categories.name: LLM Security Research
categories.summary: Multiple academic papers address defensive strategies for LLM and RAG systems against prompt injection attacks. Research spans layered security frameworks, multi-turn red-teaming benchmarks, and novel misdirection-based defense strategies that aim to degrade attacker feedback loops rather than simply blocking malicious inputs.

key_items.title: 3-Layer RAG Defense Framework Against Prompt Injection
key_items.detail: Proposes input gating, instruction/provenance hierarchy enforcement during context assembly, and output auditing with semantic-drift checks and structured logging feedback loops.

key_items.title: NRT-Bench: Multi-Turn Red-Teaming for LLM Agents
key_items.detail: New benchmark evaluates LLM operator agents in safety-critical control-room simulations using objective safety function loss metrics rather than LLM-judged text, revealing model-dependent and largely non-overlapping failure modes.

key_items.title: Defensive Misdirection Against Automated Jailbreak Attacks
key_items.detail: Evaluates detect-and-misdirect strategies that return intentionally misleading safe outputs to degrade automated attacker judges, bounding asymptotic success rates as query budgets grow.

categories.name: AI Agent Security Vulnerabilities
categories.summary: A critical CVE affecting the gemini-mcp-tool highlights trust boundary failures where untrusted prompt text enables local file exfiltration via @file includes and OS command injection on Windows through missing quote handling. This underscores ongoing risks in MCP-based agent tooling.

key_items.title: CVE-2026-0755: Gemini MCP Tool Command Injection
key_items.detail: Trust boundary failure allows untrusted prompts to trigger @file includes for local file reads and cmd.exe metacharacter-based command injection on Windows when quoting is missing.

categories.name: AI Safety & Governance
categories.summary: Google DeepMind published a comprehensive AI control roadmap focused on securing the future of AI agents. This strategic document signals increased industry attention to long-term agent safety and control mechanisms as autonomous AI systems become more prevalent.

key_items.title: DeepMind AI Agent Security Roadmap
key_items.detail: Strategic publication outlining DeepMind's approach to securing AI agents, addressing control mechanisms and safety considerations for increasingly autonomous systems.

top_insights: Defense-in-depth approaches for RAG systems are maturing, with research emphasizing input gating, provenance hierarchies, and output auditing as complementary layers rather than single-point solutions.
The shift from detect-and-block to detect-and-misdirect represents an emerging paradigm in LLM defense, treating attacker feedback signals as an exploitable attack surface.
MCP tooling continues to present trust boundary challenges, with prompt-to-CLI interpretation gaps creating serious command injection and file exfiltration vectors.
Major AI labs like DeepMind are publicly committing to agent security roadmaps, signaling that autonomous AI control is becoming a priority at the organizational strategy level.
Red-teaming benchmarks are evolving toward objective safety metrics rather than LLM-judged outputs, improving the reliability of robustness assessments.
